  - region "Simple English explanation of Inverse Functions":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Inverse Functions" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "An inverse undoes a one-to-one rule. If f(x)=2x+3 then f^{−1}(x)=(x−3)/2, so f(2)=7 and f^{−1}(7)=2. Inverse is not the reciprocal 1/f(x). A useful rule is Inverse rule: f^-1(f(x))=x. You can learn Inverse Functions by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Replace f(x) by y, swap x and y, solve for y, then check f^{−1}(f(x))=x. Example: Is the inverse of f the reciprocal 1/f? Inverse undoes the rule. Not 1/f(x). So the answer is no."
    - paragraph: "In real life, temperature conversion: Celsius and Fahrenheit formulas undo each other. Watch out: Writing inverse as 1/f(x). An inverse function reverses the rule, not just the value."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: Is the inverse of f the reciprocal 1/f?
      - generic "Compare your answer"
